newsitem.title: CHILE: Endesa to appeal conditions for Ralco dam.
newsitem.headline: Endesa to appeal conditions for Ralco dam.

text.p: Private power utility Endesa will appeal the conditions set by the National Environmental Commission (Conama) for approval of its Ralco dam project on the Bio Bio River.
Endesa called the conditions set by Conama "inappropriate and discriminatory," saying they went beyond what both sides agreed and that Endesa will appeal them.
"The Conama resolution has...demands that go beyond the recommendations that emerged from the studies and reference terms agreed between Endesa and Conama," said Endesa in a statement.
"Endesa...will proceed to present an appeal against Conama's Board of Directors," it said.

Conama granted Endesa a license to begin building the 570 MW dam in rainy, forested southern Chile on Monday on the condition that Endesa follow through on plans to relocate about 700 Pehuenche Indians whose ancestral lands will be flooded by the dam.

Conama also ordered Endesa to create a wildlife sanctuary covering 3,400 hectares -- about equal to the area that will be flooded -- to guarantee species preservation in the area, which includes rare temperate rain forest.
The dam has been strongly opposed by Chilean indigenous groups and environmentalists in both Chile and abroad.

Opposition to the dam reached the top echeleons of the World Bank, one of the dam's original funders. The bank complained early this year that Endesa was not living up to its environmental commmitments. Endesa then paid back the $150 million it owed the World Bank and took out a loan with a German bank.
